diagnosis_explanation: Your thyroid gland is bigger than normal. This can cause problems. Your doctor will help you manage this.
medication_rationale:
Synthroid:
This medicine is thyroid hormone. It replaces hormones your thyroid gland makes. Your doctor gave it to help with your goiter. You should feel more energetic as it works. You might feel more warm or sweat a little. This is normal. Call your doctor if you have chest pain. Also call if you feel very restless or have trouble sleeping.

Vicodin:
This medicine is for pain relief. It will help you feel more comfortable. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. This is common when it first starts working. Do not drive or use machines if you feel sleepy. Call your doctor if your pain does not get better. Also call if you feel very confused or have trouble breathing.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and have some neck soreness.
- Rest often and move around your house slowly.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 5 pounds.
- Your goal this week is to take short walks inside.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or swallowing.
- Call your doctor if your neck swells suddenly.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy may start to slowly increase.
- You can do light activities like getting dressed.
- Avoid any heavy lifting or straining.
- Your goal this week is to walk a bit longer each day.
- Watch for any new or worsening pain in your neck.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101°F.

**Week 3:**
- You should feel more comfortable moving around.
- You can try some light housework like washing dishes.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes daily.
- Watch for changes in your voice, like hoarseness.
- Call your doctor if you have persistent nausea or vomiting.

**Week 4:**
- You may notice your energy levels improving further.
- You can start to do more of your normal daily activities.
- Keep lifting no more than 5 pounds.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for short periods.
- Watch for any signs of low calcium, like tingling lips.
- Call your doctor if you have trouble speaking or a croaky voice.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel a steady improvement over several weeks.
- Listen to your body and rest when you need to.
- Keep your follow-up appointments with your doctor.
- Slowly increase your activity as you feel able.
- You should be able to return to most normal activities in about 6 weeks.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Breathing trouble: Your airway may be blocked.
- Cannot swallow food: Your throat may be closing.
- Sudden vision loss: This needs urgent care now.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Trouble breathing with activity: Your airway may be tight.
- Painful lump in your neck: This needs a doctor's check.
- Voice changes that worsen: Your nerves may be pressed.
- Neck lump grows fast: This could be serious.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
